title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck works with an abstract structure (F, ≤, ≪, //). F is a set of 'formes' (subobjects or pieces of a tame space). ≤ is inclusion, ≪ is a strict, interior-type inclusion, and // is a symmetric 'disjointness' relation. M ⊂ F and L ⊂ F are distinguished subsets (roughly 'model' pieces and 'points'), and omb(X) is the 'shadow' of X. As on pp. 61-64, the relation // defines a Galois polarity on subsets. For A ⊂ F, cosupp_F(A) = {G ∈ F | G // F for all F ∈ A}, and supp_F(A) = cosupp_F(cosupp_F(A)). The 'supports' are the closed sets of this polarity. They form Σ°_F, a complete lattice carrying an orthocomplement ('complémentaire'). Page 64 already asked whether it is distributive, i.e. Boolean.

Crossed-out start. When L carries //, there is a pair of canonical maps Σ°_M ⇄ Σ_L = P(L). One direction is A ↦ A∩L; the other is S ↦ A_S = {X ∈ M | omb(X) ⊂ S}. This anticipates the 'quasi-ensembliste' case of p. 66, where x //_L y just means x ≠ y, so that every subset of L is a support.

Main content: generalisation to an arbitrary 'dense' subset Λ ⊂ F.
- Definition: omb_Λ(F) = {X ∈ Λ | X ≪ F}.
- Axiom Disj_Λ: for all F, G ∈ F, F // G holds iff X // G for every X ∈ omb_Λ(F). So disjointness is detected by the Λ-elements lying ≪-inside F.
- For A ⊂ F, put omb_Λ(A) = ∪_{F∈A} omb_Λ(F) ⊂ Λ.
- Directly from Disj_Λ: cosupp_F(A) = cosupp_F(omb_Λ A).
- If A is closed for ≪ (as used here, X ≪ F ∈ A implies X ∈ A), then omb_Λ(A) relates to Λ∩A. Grothendieck writes omb_Λ(A) = Λ∩A, adding that in general only one inclusion holds.
- Hence cosupp_F(A) = cosupp_F(A∩Λ), and so supp_F(A) = supp_F(A∩Λ), for such A.
- Without the closedness hypothesis one still has supp_F(A) = supp_F(omb_Λ(A)).

Where it leads (p. 66). There is a bijection Σ°_F ≅ Σ°_Λ, given by A ↦ A∩Λ = omb_Λ(A) and S ↦ supp_F S = {F | omb_Λ(F) ⊂ S}. It respects inclusion and complements. One wants Λ as small as possible, ideally the 'points' L (which needs axiom AtL2), giving Σ_F ≅ Σ_M ≅ Σ_L.

Purpose. The aim is to show that the 'support' lattice of an analysis-situs structure can be computed from a small dense family of pieces, ultimately from points. This identifies abstract supports with genuine subsets of a point set in the quasi-set-theoretic case.

Modern content. This is the standard fact about polarities and dense subsets: an orthogonality relation restricted to a 'dense' subset gives an isomorphic ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets. The closest familiar instance is that RO(P) ≅ RO(D) for D dense in a forcing poset P, with // as incompatibility.
errors: The inclusion between omb_Λ(A) and Λ∩A is stated loosely. Downward ≪-closedness of A gives omb_Λ(A) ⊂ Λ∩A. The reverse inclusion would need every X ∈ Λ∩A to be ≪ some element of A, which is not implied.

Only the inclusion omb_Λ(A) ⊂ Λ∩A ⊂ A is actually needed for the conclusion. Since cosupp is antitone, cosupp(A) ⊂ cosupp(A∩Λ) ⊂ cosupp(omb_Λ A) = cosupp(A). So cosupp_F(A) = cosupp_F(A∩Λ) is correct even if the claimed equality omb_Λ(A) = Λ∩A fails.
Notational slip: 'pour toute partie A ∈ F' should read A ⊂ F.

ideas.what: Supports as closed sets of the Galois polarity defined by a disjointness relation, with complementation given by the orthogonal.
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space / polarity; complete ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets (regular open algebra analogue)
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished 'Analysis situs' notes (cote 156), as far as known

ideas.what: Axiom Disj_Λ: disjointness of F from G is detected by the Λ-elements ≪-inside F, hence cosupp(A) = cosupp(omb_Λ A) and supp(A) = supp(A∩Λ).
ideas.modern_name: Dense subset of a separative poset / dense sub-orthogonality space inducing an isomorphism of completions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in forcing and Boolean completion theory (Cohen, Scott–Solovay, 1960s)

ideas.what: Comparison Σ°_M ⇄ P(L) via A ↦ A∩L and S ↦ {X | omb(X) ⊂ S} (crossed out here, developed on p. 66 with Λ = L).
ideas.modern_name: Representing a support lattice as subsets of a point set (spatiality / atomicity)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone-type representation; atomic complete Boolean algebras ≅ power sets

missed.claim: Grothendieck's lattice of 'supports' with the density axiom Disj_Λ is exactly the regular-open / Boolean-completion construction of forcing, with // as incompatibility and Λ a dense subset. He does not mention this link, and his question on p. 64 about distributivity corresponds to the ortholattice-versus-Boolean dichotomy in orthogonality spaces.
missed.quote: Soit F∈F, omb_Λ(F) = {X∈Λ | X ≪ F}. Disj_Λ : Alors pour tout G∈F, F // G ⟺ ∀X∈omb_Λ(F), X // G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only of mild interest to anyone formalising Grothendieck's tame-topology 'analysis situs' program: known results on orthogonality spaces and dense subposets would apply directly. Mathematically the statement itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a correct but routine Galois-connection argument within an unpublished axiomatic framework for tame topology. The framework itself is little known, but the specific result is a standard density lemma.
transcription_corrections: 'Cette relation entre semi-ouverts dans F, et ouverts dans M' should likely read 'entre supports dans F, et supports dans M'. The image suggests 'supports' in both places.
'pour toute partie A∈F' should read A⊂F as written in the image context.
'en reprenant les cosmpr[?]ots' is probably 'en reprenant les supports'.
On the neighbouring page 66, 'rapports' is probably 'supports' throughout.
